title: [C19T2] - Harbour in 2000 and today
prompt: The plans below show a harbour in 2000 and how it looks today. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The maps compare the layout of Porth Harbour in 2000 with the present day.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, several significant changes have been made to this harbour, particularly in the arrangement of boat facilities and the development of new amenities. The most notable transformation is the conversion of the castle into a hotel, along with the addition of commercial facilities.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the northeast section in 2000, there was a dock to serve passenger ferries, and a public beach located along the eastern shoreline. In the present-day layout, the dock area has been extended with two additional docks to provide better ferry services, while the public beach remains unchanged.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the western and southern areas, in 2000, these sections featured a marina for private yachts, some shower and toilet facilities, and two car parks connected to the main road. Some fishing boats were stationed in a dedicated area, and a lifeboat station was positioned along the southern shore, with a disused castle standing at the peninsula's end. Up to the present, the marina has been relocated southward, and fishing boats have been moved closer to the dock. A new complex of cafes and shops has been established between the lifeboat station and the marina. The most substantial change is the transformation of the castle into a hotel, with a new access road designated for hotel use only. Additional shower and toilet facilities have also been constructed to accommodate increased visitor numbers.
